A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion differentiable resampling work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian-mixture resampling, linear Gaussian filtering, prey–predator learning, and pendulum-image experiments in Section 4 and Appendices F–J.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds results for a second pendulum regime, including Tables 15–16 and additional visual analyses.

M1.justification: The core ensemble-score diffusion resampler remains. V2 corrects Gaussian transition/integrator covariance factors and Algorithm 2's likelihood aggregation. Appendix J also introduces an additive-noise transition model for the second regime, replacing noise concatenation at the network input for that setting. These are limited corrections and adaptations.

E1.justification: The four task families remain. Appendix J adds a pendulum regime with process-noise covariance 0.1 diag(0,1), alongside the original 0.01 I2 regime. Coverage expands within the existing simulated pendulum environment, without adding a new dataset or application domain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain OT, Gumbel-Softmax, Soft, and, where previously applicable, multinomial resampling. The second pendulum regime uses the existing OT/Gumbel/Soft comparator set. Newly cited categorical-reparameterization work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix J changes the reported original pendulum schedule from every-step resampling to adaptive resampling when ESS < N, while retaining Tables 13–14; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun. It also adds a substantially different protocol: forced resampling after j > 10, 16 particles, 1500 training iterations, and revised noise, likelihood scaling, and optimizer settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds a stress test of end-to-end learning with resampling at nearly every filtering step, plus comparative image reconstructions and another transformed-latent-trajectory case study in Figures 10–11. Existing integrator, discretization, and failure analyses remain. The new stress test changes several settings jointly.

E5.justification: Appendix J retains five independent runs for the original pendulum regime and specifies nine for the added regime; this is not an increase in the original experiment's repeats. Figure 8 newly cautions that OT's reported median in the second regime represents only one successful run. Mean-and-standard-deviation reporting already existed.

E6.justification: The added pendulum results materially expand the evidence about comparative performance and failure. Tables 15–16 report SSIM/PSNR of 0.671/17.2 for diffusion EM-SDE at T=1, K=4 versus 0.720/17.7 for Soft(0.7); OT(0.5) has only one successful run. These are new-condition results. Separately, Table 10 replaces Gumbel, Soft, and multinomial parameter-error entries around 14.14 with NaN. Most earlier scores, including Tables 13–14, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces W1 bounds with squared W2 bounds. Assumption 1 introduces strong log-concavity and explicit constraints between contraction constants; Assumption 2 changes from mean absolute score error to root-mean-square error. Proposition 1, Corollary 1, and their proofs in Appendices B–C are substantially revised, beyond notation or exposition.

C1.justification: The abstract now distinguishes benchmark outperformance from competitive end-to-end performance on image-based dynamics learning. The conclusion drops standalone resampling from its outperformance claim. The central contribution remains a training-free, differentiable diffusion resampler with a claimed consistency guarantee.

C2.justification: Appendix J substantially qualifies the interpretation of image-learning success: tempering can keep ESS high and make resampling infrequent, while the learned dynamics can ignore noise because reconstruction training need not produce a good filtering distribution. V2 also discusses Soft's stronger image metrics alongside its weight-degeneracy drawback. The latent-identifiability limitation was already present in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix J newly specifies Adam beta2/defaults and the policy for skipping up to ten consecutive non-finite updates, together with detailed settings for the added regime. Existing architecture descriptions and the code-access statement remain. Section 4.1 removes the disclosure that implementation was not fully parallelized, without establishing an actual implementation change.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds positioning against Gourevitch et al. (2026), explaining the distinction between one-hot categorical samples and samples in Euclidean space, and conditions under which the approaches coincide. Supporting citations are added or replaced. The earlier Stein and continuous-time filtering discussion is retained in Appendix K.

P1.justification: V2 makes scattered language corrections and localized rewrites of the abstract, convergence discussion, and pendulum narrative. Appendix J gains descriptive subheadings; part of related work moves to Appendix K, and takeaways move from K to L. The overall document organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds pendulum result Tables 15–16 and additional comparison plots and image panels. V1's Figure 8 loss and latent-trajectory panels are retained in v2 Figures 8 and 11, respectively, each supplemented with the second regime. Other changes mainly involve captions, table relocation, and local page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical transparency by acknowledging the original pendulum experiment's infrequent resampling, adding a frequent-resampling stress test, and qualifying performance claims. However, Appendix B replaces v1's norm bound with a squared-moment bound in Equation (19) without the corresponding adjustment to the Grönwall expression; the preceding inequality does not justify that bound as printed. Because this concerns the central convergence guarantee, the empirical and documentation benefits cannot be reliably weighed against the proof revision.
